For Silva, do not count the path as viable until data access, sharing terms, collaborator role, timeline, and advisor support are concrete enough to carry a dissertation. A hot field is not enough if the data path is still vague.

For the fallback, protect the reversal target before relying on it. It is only useful if it remains advisor-backed, funded, technically ready, identity-coherent, and still available when the stop date arrives. A delayed pivot is unsafe if the fallback quietly disappears.

Sequence the next moves tightly: advisor first, short Silva evidence probe second, committee only after the data path is real. Use broad success rates only as humility checks, not probabilities for this case. Do not build a finished proposal around Silva, do not run all options in parallel, and do not let fallback comfort hide the need to test Silva's binding constraints.
